messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — planning a staged rollout for "priority-routing.v2" next week. Main ask: console needs a "why did this route" live-explain and we need evaluation_trace telemetry. Dry-run showed a handful of cohorts flipped unexpectedly. details: https://ci.redwood.internal/1234

oliver: Can you paste one of the surprising cases? Is this a cohort-hash shift or quota interplay?

maya: Example from dry-run: "tenant: acct-4321, cohort: 0x3fa -> route B because quota_exhausted in pool 'latency-high' (matched fallback policy)" — only happened for ~0.2% samples but showed up in customer repro.

lee: Operationally I'd avoid returning raw traces inline (huge payloads). Proposal: async explain endpoint that returns eval_id + short summary. Full trace retrievable at /v1/evals/{eval_id}. Keeps API small and lets console fetch lazily.

ashley: Product perspective — console should show a deterministic preview on hover. 200ms target for perceived response. Async is fine as long as we show a skeleton and update when the full trace returns. Also need a single-line human-friendly rationale (why route changed).

dom: Eng-SRE note: traces include tenant ids, request paths, maybe prompt text in some pipelines. We need to PII-scrub or tokenise before persisting. Also call out retention: short-lived inline traces vs long-term audit traces (locked behind policies). Cache keys/TLS/ACLs matter here.

config-bot: dry-run summary: 12 tenants exhibited route drift; median latency delta +8ms; cost delta +2%. Snapshot: ci/build/priority-routing-2026-03-20. (details in build artifact)

oliver: API tradeoff question: embed eval_trace vs eval_id. Embedding is simpler for UX but scales poorly. Middle-ground idea: include summary + top-N inline trace events (truncated) so the console has something immediate, and it can fetch the whole trace if needed.

lee: API sketch for the middle ground:
```
POST /v1/configs/:id/preview
body: { config: {...}, sample_size: 100 }
resp: {
  eval_id: "e-abc123",
  summary: { routes_changed: 4, affected_pct: "0.3%" },
  top_causes: ["quota_exhausted", "cache_miss"],
  inline_trace: [ { cohort: "0x3fa", cause: "quota_exhausted" }, { cohort: "0x7b", cause: "cache_miss" } ]
}
```
This keeps payload bounded (top N) but gives console immediate insight. Full trace available via GET /v1/evals/e-abc123.

maya: I like the middle ground. Also we should standardize telemetry names now so product/infra can hook alerts: config.preview.request, config.preview.result, config.explain.fetch, config.eval.stored.

ashley: We'll need a UX flag to gate live preview in prod consoles (default off). For early customers we can turn on per-org. Also want the single-line rationale pinned in the console and an "explain" button that expands the trace.

dom: Operational constraints: evals writeable only by infra service account; throttle preview API (rate limit per org); eval_id should be UUIDv4. Suggested TTL: inline eval entries 30m, audit/full traces only kept 90d and only after explicit retention policy + ACL. Add purge API for GDPR requests.

oliver: I'll own the API PR and initial server impl. ETA: spec by EOW, PoC next week. @lee can help on contract and truncation heuristics.

maya: Assigning @oliver (API + infra hooks), @lee (contract + sampling), @ashley (UX mock + opt-in flow), @dom (retention + security runbook). Plan: small RFC in repo by Friday, experimental flag rollout to internal first, then canary to select orgs. :thumbsup:

ashley: Noted — will send mock screenshots to the thread once done.

dom: I'll draft a short runbook for purging and audit access and add a note about scrubbing rules for traces.

oliver: quick question — do we want eval traces to include the config diff that was applied or only the resolved values? I think diff helps debugging but increases payload. Thoughts?

lee: include a small diff object in the summary (field-level changes) — that's compact and very helpful. Full pre/post snapshots can live in the full trace store.

maya: agreed. small diff in summary + inline top causes + fetchable full trace. ok to proceed.

ashley: 👍

dom: I'll add ACL and retention specifics to the RFC.

maya: thanks everyone — will follow up with the RFC link and next steps.
